# Installation that explains itself when it fails {#sec-installation}

- What is left of the installation cluster once the TensorFlow unpin
  shipped. Grouping label: the `installation` cluster.
- The theme is diagnosis, not capability: when installing greta or
  loading its Python stack goes wrong, greta should say *what* failed
  and *what to do next*, rather than reporting the same message
  whatever the cause.

**The unpin has shipped.** greta now uses the Keras 3 optimiser API
and supports TensorFlow 2.18 to 2.21, TensorFlow Probability 0.25, and
Python 3.10 or later. That closed most of what used to sit in this
milestone.

What survives is the part the unpin never addressed. greta's install
path writes a logfile nobody reads, its `cli` output is truncated in
places, and a failure to load Python, TensorFlow or TensorFlow
Probability used to produce one undifferentiated message. Some of that
is already better - the load-path error now names which component
failed ([#825](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/825)) - but
the remaining eight issues are all versions of the same complaint:
greta knows more about the failure than it tells you.

None of these block anything else in the plan, and none depend on each
other. Any subset is a shippable patch.

## Sprint item: retire the `#TF1/2` code markers {#sec-tf-markers}

*This needs no new issue: it is
[#745](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/745).* What follows is the
approach for that issue, not separate work.

Roughly 40 `#TF1/2` markers remain in `R/` (`grep -rn "TF1/2" R/`),
flagging code written for the TF1→TF2 transition that may now be dead,
redundant, or wrong under a modern TF. [#745](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/745) asks for them to be bundled
into issues; that work belongs to the unpin, since the unpin is when
their assumptions are actually tested.

**Approach.** Sweep the markers during the unpin, sort each into
delete / keep-and-unmark / file-as-issue, and close [#745](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/745) once the
sweep is done — not before.


## [Issue #546](https://github.com/greta-dev/greta/issues/546)

- 2022-08-09
- Up Next, TF2, impact-1
- The retracing warning in TF2.
- problem: real, intermittent, TF-version-sensitive; the maintainer wants it resolved early.
- finding: `tf_function` retracing is triggered by shape/dtype churn; this milestone is inside the `tf_function` plumbing anyway (unpin), so it is the cheapest moment to investigate. Not sweep-closable - it records real behaviour.
- fix: stabilise input signatures on the compiled functions (`R/dag_class.R:50`, `R/sampler_class.R:74`); if unreproducible, diagnose and document.
- priority: high (explicit maintainer steer).
